content.text:
Yes. The real issue is that Recent mixes two concepts:

- Conversations and Behaviors are “pieces of work” with descriptive titles.
- ChatGPT, Claude, and Lobu CLI are merely “sources/apps.”

Current `origin/main` confirms MCP rows are grouped per connected client and labeled only with `client.title`. Richer information—call count, tool names, failures, time—already exists in Activity, but is not shown in the sidebar.

### What other products do

| Product pattern | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Copilot | Automatically generates a semantic chat title, with manual rename. [Microsoft](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/frequently-asked-questions-about-microsoft-365-copilot-chat) |
| Claude | Gives conversations titles and supports renaming. [Anthropic](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/8230524-how-can-i-delete-or-rename-a-conversation) |
| Gemini | Recent chats can be renamed, pinned, and searched. [Google](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13666746?hl=en-GB) |
| ChatGPT | Search covers both conversation titles and content, compensating when titles are imperfect. [OpenAI](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10056348-how-do-i-search-my-chat-history-in-chatgpt) |
| Slack Activity | Makes the message/action primary and its channel, person, or app contextual; also offers dense and detailed layouts. [Slack](https://slack.com/help/articles/19693583638803-Get-your-work-done-from-the-Activity-view) |

The common rule is: **title the work, show the product as metadata**.

### What I would do in Lobu

Instead of:

> ChatGPT

Show:

> Investigated Social Interest Radar  
> ChatGPT · 8 calls · 4m ago

Other examples:

> Updated the hourly collaborator Behavior  
> Claude · 3 calls

> Queried recent customer activity  
> Lobu CLI · 1 call

If Lobu cannot safely infer the purpose:

> Used search and query tools  
> ChatGPT · 5 calls

The icon still communicates the source. Failures or pending approvals could become small badges.

More fundamentally, MCP entries should either:

1. Represent individual recent sessions/work contexts, consistent with chats and Behaviors; or
2. Move into a separate “Connected apps” section if they remain one permanent shortcut per product.

I strongly prefer the first.

### Feasibility

This is feasible, but MCP itself only provides client implementation identity such as ChatGPT or Claude—not a standard human task title. Lobu therefore has to materialize one from its own activity data. That conclusion follows from the official MCP `clientInfo` contract. [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/schema)

The safe implementation would:

- Generate a deterministic title from tool display names and approved structural fields.
- Store it when the invocation/session is written, avoiding read-time history aggregation.
- Never derive sidebar text from raw sensitive arguments.
- Keep the current app name as secondary attribution.
- Later add rename, pin, and search.

A good first version could simply promote the existing Activity summary—call count and humanized tool names—into a second sidebar line. The complete version should make MCP sessions first-class Recent items with semantic titles.

content.text: The sample is already revealing a second problem beyond titles: one OAuth client registration can span multiple organizations, but the sidebar orders it by the client’s global `last_seen_at`. In Community, “Lobu” can therefore look recently active because it was used in Buremba, even when Community itself had no matching recent session. I’m verifying that against membership/UI state before treating it as a design conclusion.

Verdict: on real production data, the two-line design would be substantially clearer. But the bigger fix is making Recent represent org-scoped work sessions—not permanent app shortcuts.

I checked Buremba, Lobu Community, and Lobu Team live against production image `20260802-154808-001828`. Database inspection was read-only.

### Buremba

Today it mixes:

- `Claude`
- `Social interest radar (X + LinkedIn)`
- `Lobu`
- `Lobu CLI`
- `ChatGPT`
- Raw prompts such as `Return ONLY a JSON object…`
- Test prompts such as `Reply with exactly: OK`

A representative improved version:

```text
Investigated Lobu data
Claude · 66 calls · 10 failed · just now

Social interest radar (X + LinkedIn)
Behavior · completed recently

Searched and queried Lobu
Lobu · 3 calls · 1 failed

Ran an SDK workflow
Lobu CLI · 1 call

Hourly Task Collaborator
Behavior · hourly

Ran an SDK workflow
ChatGPT · 1 call · failed

Social radar digest JSON test
personal-finance · chat

AI infrastructure prose test
personal-finance · chat

Exact-response reference test
personal-finance · chat
```

The Behavior titles are already good. The weak areas are app-only rows and raw test prompts.

### Lobu Community

Current Recent is:

- `Lobu`
- A long Stripe-payment prompt
- `naber`
- `how many people are in our CRM?`
- `which users do we have`
- `heyo`
- `HN engagement — draft replies`

Improved:

```text
Stripe payment failure for Acme Corp
Slack · Builder

CRM headcount
Slack · crm

CRM user list
Slack · crm

naber
Slack · crm

HN engagement — draft replies
Behavior · last completed Jul 15
```

Short human messages such as `naber` and `heyo` should probably remain unchanged. Generating elaborate titles for them would make the list feel less natural.

### Lobu Team

This organization demonstrates the largest gain. Almost every current title is a raw command:

- `Run read-only checks: pwd; command -v node…`
- `Use the bash tool to run this exact command…`
- `printf '%s'…`
- `echo hello > /tmp/x.txt…`

Improved:

```text
Runtime capability check
Developer · chat

Conversation ID and URL lookup
Builder · chat

Create a GitHub resource through the API
Builder · chat

Write repository content through the GitHub API
Builder · chat

JSON file round-trip test
Builder · chat

Multi-command execution test
Builder · chat

Shell file-write test
Builder · chat
```

### Important production finding

There is also an org-scoping defect in the current MCP recency model.

Community displays `Lobu` first, but that registration’s latest Community tool call was July 20. Its global client record was refreshed by Buremba on August 2, so activity in Buremba makes the same client appear recently active in Community.

Therefore the implementation should:

- Materialize recency per organization and session.
- Display one row per recent MCP work session.
- Use the product—Claude, ChatGPT, Lobu CLI—as secondary attribution.
- Generate conversation titles after the first turn.
- Leave already-good Behavior names and short natural messages alone.
- Fall back to deterministic tool summaries when no safe semantic context exists.

A first version can produce titles like `Queried Lobu data` from safe SDK method names. More specific titles such as `Investigated Social Radar notifications` require a bounded semantic-title step over authorized task context; that intent cannot be reliably recovered from sanitized tool names alone.

content.text:
Yes—but “we” means ChatGPT, not Lobu.

The exact boundary is:

- ChatGPT knows the conversation title.
- MCP sends Lobu `_meta["openai/session"]`, an anonymized stable conversation ID—but **not the title**. The documented client metadata has no conversation-title field. [OpenAI reference](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/reference#_meta-fields-the-client-provides)
- Lobu currently ignores `tools/call.params._meta`, so it even loses that stable conversation ID.
- Lobu instead stores the app name (`ChatGPT`) and a transport session UUID. Production shows those transport UUIDs changing between calls, so they cannot identify the ChatGPT conversation.

Therefore the sidebar only has enough information to display **ChatGPT**.

So there is a real Lobu gap: we should capture `openai/session`, group calls into one conversation, and generate a Lobu-side title from the first meaningful request—giving something like:

> ChatGPT · Investigate customer churn

But showing ChatGPT’s exact existing title is impossible until ChatGPT exposes that title through MCP. No code was changed; this was diagnosis only.

The topic should be primary; the originating app belongs in the icon/subtitle:


For titles:

- **ChatGPT:** capture `_meta["openai/session"]` to group calls, then generate a short Lobu-side title from the first meaningful request. OpenAI provides the conversation ID but not its title. - **Lobu in Slack:** use a host-provided thread/channel title when available; otherwise generate from the first request.
- **True native Lobu calls:** use `sourceContext.conversationId` to resolve the existing exact `conversations.title`.

Create a write-time materialized `mcp_client_threads` table. Do not put it in:

- `oauth_clients.metadata`: registration/app-level and currently shared across activity.
- `mcp_sessions`: temporary HTTP transport recovery state.
- `events` or encrypted request snapshots: append-only/retention-oriented audit data, not a sidebar index.
- `conversations`: external MCP tool activity has no Lobu transcript and different routing semantics. Native Lobu calls should reference an existing conversation instead.

```text
organization_id

external_thread_key_hash    # openai/session or another stable host ID
source_conversation_id      # native Lobu, nullable

title

first_activity_at
last_activity_at

last_tool_name
```

Capture should happen in the `CallToolRequestSchema` handler in [mcp-handler.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:289), where `request.params._meta` is still available. Parse only allowlisted fields into a per-call context—never persist the entire `_meta` object.

```text

hostTitle: "ChatGPT"
```

You’re right—we should show channel, workspace, project, or repository whenever that context exists. The current omission is structural, not a good UX decision.

Current MCP Recent rows represent an entire OAuth client registration. Lobu stores:

- Registered app: `Lobu`
- Driver: `Slack MCP Client`
- User and last activity

It does not capture per-call host context, so everything collapses into one “Lobu” row.

There is one Slack-specific limitation: Lobu’s Slack integration uses Dynamic Client Registration, and Slackbot runs from a DM. Slack documents `_meta.slack` user/team identity for its separate Slack-identity authentication mode, but does not document channel/thread context for DCR calls. [Slack MCP client documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slackbot-mcp-client/)

So the intended hierarchy should be:

```text
Primary:   task/thread title
Secondary: app · workspace · channel/container
```

Examples:

```text
Social interest radar
ChatGPT

Investigate failed deployment
Lobu via Slackbot

Launch coordination
Slack · Acme · #product · thread

Fix checkout regression
Claude Code · lobu

Review PR #2436
Lobu CLI · Lobu-AI/lobu
```

The normalized stored context should include:

```text
host_surface       # chatgpt, slackbot, claude, cli
workspace_id/name
container_kind     # channel, repository, project, chat
container_id/name
thread_id/name
source_url
context_source     # verified, host_meta, generated
```

Implementation rules:

- Direct Slack/Telegram/etc. conversations already have verified `sourceContext` containing channel/team/connection IDs. Enrich their existing `conversations` rows with resolved display labels.
- MCP clients should expose per-call context through `_meta`; MCP explicitly supports namespaced metadata extensions. [MCP metadata specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic)
- Parse allowlisted provider-specific fields in [mcp-handler.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts:289), then materialize them in `mcp_client_threads`.
- Never persist the entire `_meta` object or trust display context for authorization.
- If a client supplies no location, fall back to the generated task title plus host—e.g. `Investigate failed deployment · Lobu via Slackbot`.

For the screenshot specifically, the immediate honest improvement is **“Lobu via Slackbot.”** A channel cannot currently be shown because Slackbot’s documented DCR request does not provide one. No code was changed.

No—Lobu is not on the latest MCP protocol.

Lobu currently advertises `2025-03-26` in [constants.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/core/src/constants.ts:28). Although Bun resolves SDK `1.29.0`, that is still the v1 SDK line. The current protocol is `2026-07-28`, and the official TypeScript SDK v2 is now stable with split server/client packages. [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest), [TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk#readme)

### Recommended single-line Recent design

Keep the existing row height. Put the useful title first and source context afterward on the same line:

```text
⌁  Claude
☷  Social interest radar
▣  Review MCP recent titles · Lobu
▣  Investigate deployment issue · Lobu CLI
◉  Improve Recent conversation titles · ChatGPT
#  Launch coordination · Slack #product
☷  Hourly Task Collaborator
▢  Return ONLY a JSON object…
```

The implementation should use one flex row with `white-space: nowrap`. The title takes the available space and ellipsizes; the source/context suffix is capped to roughly 40% and also ellipsizes. Hovering exposes the complete text. No subtitle and no additional vertical height.

### How web conversations fit

Native Lobu web conversations already have a real conversation record and `conversation.title`, so they remain the cleanest rows:

```text
▢  Return ONLY a JSON object…
▢  Write ~3000 characters of planning…
```

They do not need `· Web` because the conversation icon and click destination already make that clear.

MCP-originated rows become:

```text
◉  Improve Recent conversation titles · ChatGPT
▣  Review connector authorization · Lobu
⌘  Repair migration command · Lobu CLI
```

Slack-originated rows include their location when available:

```text
#  Prepare launch announcement · #marketing
#  Diagnose production alert · #incidents › thread
```

Click behavior:

- Native web conversation → opens the actual Lobu chat.
- Slack conversation → opens the channel/thread when a URL is available.
- MCP conversation → opens Activity filtered to that external thread, not merely every call from “ChatGPT”.
- Behavior → opens the Behavior page.

### What storing the richer context requires

At MCP ingestion time, capture a small allowlisted context object—not the entire `_meta` payload:

```ts
{
  externalThreadId,
  title,
  source: "chatgpt" | "lobu" | "lobu-cli" | "slack",
  container: {
    type: "channel" | "thread" | "project",
    id,
    label
  },
  sourceUrl
}
```

First-party Lobu clients should send this through a namespaced MCP metadata field such as `ai.lobu/conversation`. Because we control both ends, Lobu can provide the exact conversation ID and title.

For other clients:

- ChatGPT provides a stable `openai/session` identity, but not its visible conversation title. We therefore generate a short title from the first meaningful request.
- Slack’s documented `_meta.slack` currently guarantees user/team identity, not necessarily channel/thread identity. We display the channel when our Slack path knows it or the host provides it; we must not fabricate it. [Slackbot MCP documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slackbot-mcp-client/)
- Unknown clients fall back to something useful such as `Search repository activity · Cursor`, then ultimately `run_sdk activity · ChatGPT`.

Materialize this into something like `mcp_client_threads` during every tool call:

- Unique by organization, authenticated client and hashed external-thread ID.
- Store generated/display title, source, container labels, source URL and last activity.
- Index by organization and last activity.
- Never reconstruct Recent using `GROUP BY` over the growing events table.
- Never use client-provided titles or container fields for authorization.

Owletto then receives explicit fields such as `title`, `sourceLabel`, `contextLabel`, `sourceUrl`, and `lastActivityAt`. It only merges and renders them.

### MCP upgrade scope

The MCP v2 migration is more than changing the version constant:

- Replace `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` v1 with the new `@modelcontextprotocol/server` and related v2 packages.
- Serve `2026-07-28` using the new stateless, self-contained request handler.
- Preserve a legacy 2025 path while ChatGPT, Slack and other clients transition.
- Move client identity and capabilities from initialization/session state to each request’s `_meta` envelope.
- Stop treating `Mcp-Session-Id` as the durable client/thread identity.
- Rework authentication/request context and test cross-replica routing.
- Run compatibility tests against Lobu, Lobu CLI, ChatGPT and Slackbot.

The v2 handler can serve modern and legacy traffic from one endpoint, which gives us a safe transition path. [Official v2 migration guide](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/docs/migration/support-2026-07-28.md)

I would ship the title/context storage independently of the MCP v2 migration. The former fixes Recent immediately and is protocol-version-neutral; the latter changes transport and session architecture. This assessment is against the freshly fetched current `origin/main`, not the older checkout state.

content.text:
We currently have three different things that were being conflated:

1. **MCP application name** — “ChatGPT”, “Lobu CLI”. We have this.
2. **Lobu conversation title** — title of a web/Slack/Telegram agent conversation. We generally have this.
3. **The MCP host’s conversation title** — the title ChatGPT displays in its own sidebar. We do not automatically have this.

An SDK operation can close the third gap for clients willing or able to provide it.

### Proposed client contract

Something like:

```ts
await client.context.setConversation({
  title: "Improve Recent conversation titles",
  location: {
    kind: "channel",
    id: "C012345",
    label: "#product",
  },
  url: "https://…",
});
```

The server should bind this operation to the caller’s current MCP context. The client must not pass a raw Lobu session ID or update another client’s thread.

First-party clients can call it automatically:

- Lobu web: when a conversation is created, renamed, or auto-titled.
- Lobu CLI: when its task/thread name becomes known.
- Slack integration: after resolving the channel and thread.
- Other MCP hosts: whenever they support the operation.

For ChatGPT, we can expose and document the operation, but we cannot force ChatGPT to call it or assume its agent knows the title shown in ChatGPT’s sidebar.

### What Lobu has today

Native Lobu conversations already live in the durable `conversations` table. Their current title is essentially the first inbound message, truncated to 200 characters, and the first non-null value wins. That explains titles such as:

```text
Return ONLY a JSON object, …
Write ~3000 characters of pla…
```

The existing ClientSDK has:

```ts
client.conversations.list(...)
client.conversations.get(...)
client.conversations.send(...)
```

It does not currently have a rename/update-title action.

MCP client activity is separate. Today it knows:

- MCP session ID
- Client ID and application name
- User and agent
- Tools called
- Call/error counts
- Activity timestamps

It has no stored conversation title.

### Single-line result by source

| Source | Best information | Sidebar row |
|---|---|---|
| Lobu web | Explicit/generated conversation title | `[Lobu] Improve Recent titles` |
| Lobu CLI | Client-provided task/thread title | `[CLI] Investigate MCP metadata` |
| ChatGPT MCP | Client-provided title; otherwise Lobu activity label | `[ChatGPT] Investigate deployment failure` |
| Claude/Cursor/Codex MCP | Same opt-in context contract | `[client logo] Review authorization flow` |
| Slack channel thread | Friendly channel plus thread subject | `[Slack] #product · Review launch plan` |
| Slack DM | Person/group name plus subject | `[Slack] Burak · Review launch plan` |
| Telegram/Discord/Teams | Friendly chat/channel/topic plus subject | `[logo] Engineering · Deployment failure` |
| Behavior | Existing Behavior name | `[Behavior] Hourly Task Collaborator` |

The brackets represent logos; product names would not appear in the actual text.

### Slack specifically

Yes—a Slack thread is effectively one Lobu conversation. Internally its identity is currently shaped like:

```text
slack:C012345:1700000000.123456
```

That is useful for routing but terrible as a title.

The parts should remain separate:

```text
platform: slack
container_id: C012345
container_label: #product
thread_id: 1700000000.123456
title: Review launch plan
```

Owletto composes them into one line:

```text
[Slack logo] #product · Review launch plan
```

For a DM:

```text
[Slack logo] Burak · Review launch plan
```

We already receive the channel ID, workspace ID, thread identity and often a permalink. The missing step is resolving and materializing the friendly channel/person label once at ingress. We should never make the sidebar parse or display the raw routing ID.

The storage priority should be:

1. User-renamed title
2. Client/host-provided title
3. Platform thread subject or first message
4. Lobu-generated activity label
5. Friendly container alone
6. Raw ID only in diagnostics—not in Recent

This gives us one consistent Recent model without pretending that Lobu automatically knows ChatGPT’s private sidebar title.

Yes: **the latest meaningful tool**, not necessarily the first tool and not literally every protocol call.

If an explicit client title exists, it remains stable. Otherwise the row tracks what the MCP thread most recently did:

```text
[ChatGPT] Search memory for deployment failures
[Cursor] Update customer classification
[Claude] Query Slack conversations
```

We should ignore bookkeeping calls such as initialization, title updates, discovery, polling, and approvals when choosing the label.

## Gaps to consolidate

| Current gap | Consolidated behavior |
|---|---|
| MCP client registration is treated like a conversation | Registrations stay under Connectors; Recent contains actual MCP threads/activity |
| MCP sessions have no title or thread metadata | Add an explicit current-context SDK operation |
| MCP Recent is derived using `GROUP BY` over audit events | Materialize an `mcp_client_threads` row on every meaningful call |
| Transport session ID is treated as conversation identity | Prefer host conversation ID, `openai/session`, or verified source context; transport session is only fallback |
| Lobu conversation title is just the first 200 characters | Support explicit/generated title plus provenance |
| Slack location is encoded inside `slack:C123:timestamp` | Resolve and store `#channel`, DM participant, thread subject and URL |
| Different Recent item types have different UI logic | Return one normalized `RecentItem` contract and use one row renderer |
| Product names appear in text despite having logos | Logo identifies source; text contains title and optional location only |

## One normalized UI contract

The API should return every type as:

```ts
interface RecentItem {
  id: string;
  kind: "web" | "platform" | "mcp" | "behavior";
  source: string;
  displayTitle: string | null;
  activityLabel: string | null;
  locationLabel: string | null;
  titleSource: "user" | "host" | "first-message" | "generated" | null;
  updatedAt: number;
  route: RecentRoute;
}
```

Rendering becomes one rule:

```text
locationLabel · (displayTitle ?? activityLabel ?? "Recent activity")
```

The product name is never appended because the icon already provides it.

## Result for every source

```text
[Lobu]     Improve Recent titles
[ChatGPT]  Search memory for deployment failures
[Claude]   Compare customer churn metrics
[Cursor]   Update classification schema
[Slack]    #product · Improve Recent titles
[Slack]    Burak · Review deployment plan
[Telegram] Engineering · Production alert
[Behavior] Hourly Task Collaborator
```

For Slack, the thread is one conversation. Internally it remains:

```text
slack:C012345:1700000000.123456
```

But Recent receives separate fields:

```ts
{
  locationLabel: "#product",
  displayTitle: "Improve Recent titles"
}
```

## Storage without unnecessary consolidation

We should consolidate the **API and presentation model**, not force unrelated entities into one database table:

- `conversations`: continue storing Lobu web and platform conversations.
- Extend it with friendly location/title provenance and an explicit title-update path.
- `mcp_client_threads`: store MCP host threads and the latest meaningful action.
- `watchers`: remain the source for Behaviors.
- One indexed Recent query combines these bounded/materialized sources.
- One Owletto component renders them.

The ClientSDK addition would be something like:

```ts
await client.context.setConversation({
  title: "Improve Recent titles",
  location: {
    kind: "channel",
    id: "C012345",
    label: "#product",
  },
  url: "https://…",
});
```

It updates only the caller’s current context. When absent, each meaningful MCP tool invocation updates `activityLabel`. When the client later provides a real title, `displayTitle` takes precedence while the latest action can remain available in Activity details.

MCP v2 is not required for this consolidation and can remain a separate migration.

content.text:
There is one more simplification: **clients provide content; Lobu owns provenance and navigation**.

### Final trust boundary

The only agent-callable operation would be:

```ts
client.conversations.setTitle({ title })
```

That title is untrusted display text:

- Plain text only
- Length-limited
- Control characters, bidi overrides, markup and URLs removed
- Cannot alter the icon, location, route, workspace, client identity, or conversation identity
- Clicking the row always follows a Lobu-generated destination

Location must always come from Lobu:

```text
#product
Burak
Engineering
```

An agent must never be able to claim it came from `#security`, “OpenAI Support,” or another workspace.

### URLs

URLs must also be Lobu-generated—not supplied through `setTitle`.

We can safely construct destinations for:

- Lobu web conversations → Lobu conversation route
- Slack → server-known workspace/channel/thread permalink
- Behaviors → Lobu Behavior route
- Other platforms → only when their authenticated adapter has an authoritative route

We **cannot** safely construct a ChatGPT URL from `openai/session`. OpenAI documents it as an **anonymized conversation ID for correlating tool calls**, not as ChatGPT’s browser-visible conversation ID. Therefore `https://chatgpt.com/c/{openai/session}` is not a supported mapping. [OpenAI client metadata reference](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/reference#_meta-fields-the-client-provides)

A ChatGPT MCP row should open Lobu Activity filtered to that conversation:

```text
[ChatGPT] Search memory for deployment failures
```

If OpenAI later provides an explicit, verified deep-link field, we can add support then with a strict `chatgpt.com` origin allowlist.

### Smallest complete model

```ts
interface RecentItem {
  id: string;
  source: string;          // trusted; selects logo
  title: string;           // untrusted display text
  location?: string;       // trusted, server-derived
  href: string;            // trusted, server-generated
  updatedAt: number;
}
```

That is enough. We do not need client-supplied location, URLs, icons, source names, session IDs, or a generic `client.context` API.

One further safety choice: if we decide arbitrary agent-authored titles are still too deceptive, we can omit `setTitle` for generic MCP clients initially and use only curated latest-tool labels. First-party Lobu clients can supply titles through their trusted host integration rather than an agent-callable tool.

*** Update File: /Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/recent-conversation-context/db/migrations/20260803130000_events_pending_mcp_session_idx.sql

+-- That query maps the org's live pending interactions to materialized MCP
+-- conversations through their transport-session ids.
@@
--- Operational cost: CONCURRENTLY (events is the hot ~1M+ row table, so a plain
--- CREATE INDEX would block writes for the build). The predicate matches only
--- currently-pending rows, so the resulting index is small. If a deploy retry
--- hits the CONCURRENTLY + IF NOT EXISTS invalid-index trap, see
--- docs/MIGRATIONS.md.
+-- Operational cost: CONCURRENTLY (events is the hot ~1M+ row table, so a plain
+-- CREATE INDEX would block writes for the build). Heal an invalid carcass first
+-- so a crashed build can be retried safely.
+
+DO $heal$
+BEGIN
+  IF EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1
+    FROM pg_index i
+    JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
+    JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
+    WHERE n.nspname = 'public'
+      AND c.relname = 'events_pending_interaction_mcp_session'
+      AND NOT i.indisvalid
+  ) THEN
+    EXECUTE 'DROP INDEX public.events_pending_interaction_mcp_session';
+  END IF;
+END
+$heal$;
@@
 CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS events_pending_interaction_mcp_session
-  ON events (organization_id, (metadata->>'mcp_session_id'))
-  WHERE interaction_status = 'pending';
+  ON public.events (organization_id, (metadata->>'mcp_session_id'))
+  WHERE interaction_status = 'pending'
+    AND interaction_type <> 'none'
+    AND metadata->>'mcp_session_id' IS NOT NULL
+    AND superseded_by IS NULL;
@@
-DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS events_pending_interaction_mcp_session;
+DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS public.events_pending_interaction_mcp_session;
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

Yes—the Recent row is incomplete.

For MCP conversations, the API already returns `callCount`, failures, pending approvals, and last action. Recent currently ignores the count and has no real running state. It should look like:

```text
Desktop migration plan
[Claude icon] Running · 8 calls · 1 minute ago
```

Or when idle:

```text
ChatGPT conversation
[ChatGPT icon] 8 calls · Search memory · 3 minutes ago
```

“Running” needs a durable start/finish state; inferring it from recent timestamps would be unreliable. Slack/web conversations need a separate agent-turn status and tool-count materialization—the MCP count has different semantics.

- Created `#lobu-buremba-test`.

- Slack returned: “app did not respond.”

So this is an upstream Slack linking failure, not Recent hiding a valid row. I left the channel open for retesting after the `/lobu` route is fixed.

content.text: I found the existing durable primitives needed to keep this simpler and trustworthy: every agent turn already has a Postgres-backed liveness marker, and every terminal worker response already carries distinct tools used. I’m extending the write-time `conversations` projection with a latest-message lease plus exact tool-call count/last tool, then reading those indexed columns directly—no request-time run-history aggregation and no in-memory state.

content.text: The durable design will use the existing `conversations` projection, not query run history: each inbound turn replaces a per-conversation running generation keyed by message ID; worker progress refreshes that same generation; terminalization clears only matching message IDs and persists the exact call count/last tool. That prevents a late older completion from clearing a newer Slack turn.

content.text: One correctness issue surfaced in the type pass: the listing row is written before input guardrails, so marking it running there could show a rejected turn as “Running” for the lease window. I’m separating “ensure conversation exists” from “begin accepted turn” and placing the running transition immediately before the existing durable turn-timeout marker is armed.

The parent branch was pushed prematurely, so add a follow-up fix commit and only then rerun focused red-to-green, migration replay/lint, and pre-pr. Do not create the parent PR until those corrections are green.
